newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO bars Israeli goods in tit-for-tat policy.
newsitem.headline: PLO bars Israeli goods in tit-for-tat policy.

text.p: The PLO said on Sunday it was barring Israeli fruits and vegetables from entering Gaza in retaliation for an Israeli closure that prevented Palestinian produce from leaving the Strip.

"Every day we lose $500,000 as a result of the closure. We banned the import of Israeli agricultural products until Israelis lift their oppressive closure," said Abdel Jawad Saleh, the Palestinian Authority member in charge of agriculture.

Israel sealed off the Gaza Strip and West Bank on Thursday for fear of Palestinian guerrilla attacks around the anniversary of the assassination of Islamic Jihad leader Fathi Shqaqi. The militant group is believed to be behind suicide bombings in the Jewish state.
Palestinians believe Shqaqi was killed by Israeli secret agents.
"There's a closure so we're not letting them export things into Israel," said a spokesman for Israel's agriculture ministry.
"Their decision to prevent our goods from entering Gaza causes us no harm. They're the only ones who will suffer from this," the spokesman told Reuters.

At the Karni crossing between Israel and Gaza, 13 trucks loaded with produce waited for permission to cross. One driver, Abdel Aziz Bashir, showed a reporter guavas that had gone soft and said he lost $40,000 since Thursday due to the closure.
